<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="" /></noinclude><section begin=par162 />{{GHGpar-heading|162|Disjunctive Sentences}}

{{GHGmargin-letter|162|a}}
The introduction of another possible case, excluding that which preceded, is effected by {{GHGheb|text=אוֹ}} or, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=21|verse=36}}, equivalent to the Latin ''vel''; but also equivalent to ''aut'' with an exclusive antithesis, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=2|verse=16}}; so {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=27|verse=5}} {{GHGheb|text=אוֹ}}= ''it would then happen that'', for which elsewhere {{GHGheb|text=אוֹ כִי}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|162|b}}
In the sense of ''sive—sive'' we find {{GHGheb|text=אוֹ}}—{{GHGheb|text=אוֹ}}, or {{GHGheb|text=אִם}}—{{GHGheb|text=אִם}}, or {{GHGheb|text=וְאִם}}—{{GHGheb|text=אִם}} (see the examples in the Lexicon), also {{GHGheb|text=וְ}}—{{GHGheb|text=וְ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Lv|chapter=5|verse=3}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=9|verse=14}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=24|verse=7}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=2|verse=13}} ff., {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=32|verse=20}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=76|verse=7}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=34|verse=29}}, perhaps also {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=21|verse=16}} (but not {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=29|verse=9}}; cf. Delitzsch on the passage), and {{GHGheb|text=לְ}}—{{GHGheb|text=לְ}} (see {{GHGpar|143|e}}); cf. also {{GHGheb|text=גַּם}}—{{GHGheb|text=גַּם}} (in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=24|verse=44}} {{GHGheb|text=וְגַם}}—{{GHGheb|text=גַּם}}) ''both—and''; but {{GHGheb|text=גַּם לֹא}}—{{GHGheb|text=גַּם לֹא}} (in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=21|verse=26}} {{GHGheb|text=וְגַם לֹא}}—{{GHGheb|text=וְגַם לֹא}}; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Zp|chapter=1|verse=18}} {{GHGheb|text=גַּם ... לֹא}}—{{GHGheb|text=גַּם}}) ''neither—nor''. On disjunctive questions, see {{GHGpar|150|g}}.<section end=par162 />

<section begin=par163 />{{GHGpar-heading|163|Adversative and Exceptive Clauses}}

{{GHGmargin-letter|163|a}}
'''1.''' After negative sentences (especially after prohibitions) the antithesis (''but'') is introduced by {{GHGheb|text=כִּי אִם}}, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=8|verse=19}} ''and they said, Nay, but we will have a king over us''; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=1|verse=2}}, &c.; frequently also by {{GHGheb|text=כִּי}} alone, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=18|verse=15}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=19|verse=2|hidebook=1}}, or even simply connected with {{GHGheb|text=וְ}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=17|verse=5}}, {{GHGheb|text=וְהָיָה}} as perfect consecutive; 42:10; cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=5|verse=18}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|163|b}}
Rem. Sometimes the negation is only virtually contained in the preceding sentence, e.g. in the form of a rhetorical question ({{GHGbible-ref|book=Mi|chapter=6|verse=3}} f.) or of conditions which are to be regarded as not having been fulfilled ({{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=31|verse=18}}); {{GHGheb|text=כִּי}} or {{GHGheb|text=כִּי אִם}} in such cases becomes equivalent to ''nay, rather''.

{{GHGmargin-letter|163|c}}
'''2.''' {{GHGterm|Exceptive}} clauses, depending on another sentence, are introduced by {{GHGheb|text=אֶ֫פֶס כִּי|translate=except that}}, and (again after negative sentences, see a above) {{GHGheb|text=כִּי אִם}}<ref>Very probably this use of {{GHGheb|text=כִּי אִם}} arises from the original meaning ''for if, surely if'' ({{GHGheb|text=כִּי}} in an affirmative sense); so evidently in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=22|verse=22}} as a forcible resumption of the preceding {{GHGheb|text=אִם}}. Thus, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=15|verse=7}} is simply ''surely when I have been avenged of you, after that I will cease'', equivalent to, I will not cease, until I have, &c. When the exception follows, an ellipse must be assumed, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ru|chapter=3|verse=18}} ''surely'' (or ''for'') ''when he has finished it'' (then the man will rest). It is far less natural to assume such an ellipse with {{GHGheb|text=כִּי אִם|translate=but}} (before entire clauses as before single nouns); see a above.</ref> ''unless''; especially {{GHGheb|text=כִּי אִם}} with the perfect (equivalent to ''unless previously'') after imperfects which contain a declaration, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=32|verse=27}} ''I will not let thee go, except thou hast'' previously ''blessed me''; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Lv|chapter=22|verse=6}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=55|verse=10}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=65|verse=6|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Am|chapter=3|verse=7}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ru|chapter=3|verse=18}}. Finally, {{GHGheb|text=בִּלְתִּי אִם|translate=unless}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Am|chapter=3|verse=4}} (with perfect after a rhetorical question), or simply {{GHGheb|text=בִּלְתִּי}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=43|verse=3}} with a noun-clause, ''except your brother be with you''; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=10|verse=4}} after a rhetorical question, with a verbal-clause.
<section end=par163 /><noinclude>
